tools.title: Ten-Frame Builder
tools.description: Fill two ten-frames with red and yellow counters to add, take away and make ten. The number sentence changes as you build.
worksheet: Show 7 + 3. How many empty boxes are in the first ten-frame?
0 — it is full. 7 + 3 = 10
Show 9 + 4. Write it as 10 + __.
Show 8 + 5. How many yellow counters fill the first frame? How many are in the second frame?
2 fill the first frame; 3 are in the second. 8 + 5 = 13
Show 5 + 6, then 6 + 5. Are the totals the same?
Yes. Both are 11.
Make 14. Take away 6. How many are left?
Write two different ways to make 10 with red and yellow counters.
Any two pairs that make 10, for example 4 + 6 and 7 + 3
Reflect: How does a ten-frame help you add 8 + 6?
Move 2 of the 6 to fill the frame: 10 + 4 = 14.

tools.title: Tens and Ones Builder
tools.description: Build numbers to 120 with ten-rods and ones cubes, bundle 10 ones into a ten, break a ten apart, and compare two numbers with >, = and <.
worksheet: Build 46. How many tens and how many ones?
4 tens and 6 ones
Build 17 using only ones. Then bundle. What do you have now?
1 ten and 7 ones
Show 32 as 2 tens and some ones. How many ones do you need?
12 ones
Build 7 tens. What number is it?
How many tens make 100?
10 tens
Compare 58 and 85. Write >, = or <.
58 < 85, because 5 tens is less than 8 tens
Reflect: Why is 1 ten the same as 10 ones?
A ten rod is 10 ones put together, so it is worth 10.

tools.title: Equal Sign Balance
tools.description: Put cubes on both sides of a balance. When both sides are worth the same, the scale is level and the equation is true.
worksheet: Put 5 + 3 on the left. Put 6 on the right. What must you add to the right side to balance?
Is 8 = 5 + 3 true or false?
True. Both sides are 8.
Is 6 + 1 = 6 + 2 true or false? Which side goes down?
False. The right side (8) goes down because 8 is more than 7.
Find the missing number: 9 + 4 = __ + 3
Find the missing number: 7 + __ = 10 + 2
Write two different ways to balance 10 on both sides.
Any two, for example 4 + 6 = 7 + 3
Reflect: What does the equal sign mean?
Both sides are worth the same amount.

tools.title: Hundred Chart Hopper
tools.description: Hop on a chart from 1 to 120 by ones and tens. See 10 more and 10 less, and write each trip as an addition or subtraction.
worksheet: Start on 36. Hop down one row. Where do you land?
46 (10 more)
What is 10 less than 81?
Start on 4 and hop +10 again and again. Write the numbers you land on.
Start on 52. Hop +10, +10, +1. Where do you land?
Use the chart: 67 − 30 = __
What number comes after 109?
Reflect: Why does moving down one row add 10?
Each row has 10 numbers, so the number below is 10 more.

tools.title: Clock Explorer
tools.description: Move the hands of a clock by hours and half hours. See the digital time and the time in words, and notice where the hour hand points.
worksheet: Show 4:00. Where does the minute hand point?
To the 12
Show 8:30. Where is the hour hand?
Halfway between the 8 and the 9
What time is it 1 hour after 5:30?
Write half past 11 as a digital time.
At 2:30, where does the minute hand point?
To the 6
What time is it a half hour after 12:00?
Reflect: Why is the hour hand between two numbers at half past?
It moves slowly to the next hour; at half past it has gone halfway.

tools.title: Measure with Cubes
tools.description: Line up cubes end to end to measure a crayon, marker, pencil and ribbon. See why gaps and overlaps give wrong measurements, then compare the lengths.
worksheet: How many cubes long is the pencil?
7 cubes
How many cubes long is the crayon?
4 cubes
How many cubes longer is the pencil than the crayon?
3 cubes
Put the crayon, marker, pencil and ribbon in order from shortest to longest.
crayon (4), marker (6), pencil (7), ribbon (11)
Measure the pencil with gaps. How many cubes reach the end? Is that the real length?
5 cubes. No — gaps make the count too small; it is really 7.
Measure the pencil with overlapping cubes. How many cubes? Is that right?
11 cubes. No — overlaps make the count too big.
Reflect: Why must the cubes touch with no gaps and no overlaps?
So every part of the length is counted exactly once.

tools.title: Tally and Picture Graph Builder
tools.description: Collect votes for favorite fruits, show them with tally marks, a table or a picture graph, and answer how many in all, how many more and how many fewer.
worksheet: How many votes are there in all? (Apples 4, Bananas 6, Grapes 3)
How many more votes do Bananas have than Grapes?
3 more
Which fruit has the most votes?
Bananas
Add 2 votes to Apples. How many do Apples have now? Which fruits tie?
6. Apples and Bananas tie.
Draw the tally marks for 7.
One bundle of 5 (4 lines crossed by 1) and 2 more lines
How many fewer votes do Grapes have than Bananas?
3 fewer
Reflect: Why do we cross the fifth tally mark?
It makes bundles of 5, so we can count by fives.

tools.title: Equal Shares
tools.description: Cut circles, rectangles and squares into halves and fourths, color the shares, and see why parts must be the same size.
worksheet: Cut a circle into 2 equal shares. What is each share called?
A half (one half)
How many fourths make a whole rectangle?
4 fourths
Which is bigger: one half or one fourth of the same circle?
One half
A rectangle is cut into 2 parts that are not the same size. Are they halves?
No. Halves must be equal shares.
Color 2 fourths of a square. How much of the square is colored?
Two fourths, the same amount as one half
How many halves make one whole?
2 halves
Reflect: Why does cutting into more equal shares make each share smaller?
The same whole is split among more parts, so each part gets less.
